gloss: to get caught up in; to be involved in; to be dragged into

definitions.gloss: to get caught up in; to be involved in; to be dragged into
definitions.explanation: Describes being involuntarily drawn into a situation, conflict, or incident. The passive form of {巻|ま}き{込|こ}む (to involve, to drag in), emphasizing the lack of choice on the subject's part.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: I got caught up in an accident.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}のけんかに{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれてしまった。
examples.english: I got dragged into my friend's quarrel.

examples.japanese: {無関係|むかんけい}の{市民|しみん}が{紛争|ふんそう}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれることがあってはならない。
examples.english: Uninvolved civilians must never be caught up in a conflict.

notes:
The passive form of {巻|ま}き{込|こ}む (to involve, to drag in, to engulf). While {巻|ま}き{込|こ}む focuses on the agent doing the involving, {巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる emphasizes the victim's perspective — being pulled into something against one's will.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事件|じけん}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる: to get caught up in an incident
- {事故|じこ}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる: to be involved in an accident
- {争|あらそ}いに{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる: to get dragged into a dispute
- {犯罪|はんざい}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる: to get mixed up in a crime
- トラブルに{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれる: to get caught up in trouble

USAGE:
Almost always used with the particle に to mark the situation one is dragged into. Carries a strong implication that the involvement was involuntary and usually unwelcome.

ACTIVE FORM:
{巻|ま}き{込|こ}む means "to involve" or "to drag in" from the agent's perspective:
- {周|まわ}りを{巻|ま}き{込|こ}む: to involve those around you
- {他人|たにん}を{巻|ま}き{込|こ}むな: don't drag others into this
